verses.text: The first covenant had rules for worship and a holy place here on earth.
A tent was set up. Its first room was called the Holy Place. In it were the lampstand, the table and the special bread offered to God.
Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place.

It had a gold altar for burning incense, and the covenant box, which was covered with gold on every side. Inside the box was a gold jar holding manna, Aaron's walking stick that had grown buds, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
Above the box were the glorious cherubim, spreading their wings over the cover where sins were forgiven. But we cannot talk about all these things in detail now.
When everything was set up like this, the priests went into the first room every day to do their work.
But only the high priest went into the second room, and only once a year. He always took blood with him, which he offered for his own sins and for the sins the people had done without knowing.
By this the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place was not yet open while the first tent was still standing.
This is a picture for the present time. It shows that the gifts and sacrifices offered there could not make the worshipper's conscience clean and perfect.
They were only about food, drink and different kinds of washing. They were rules for the body, which lasted until the time God would set things right.
But Christ has come as the High Priest of the good things that are now here. He went through a greater and more perfect tent, not made by human hands, not part of this created world.
He did not take the blood of goats and calves. He took his own blood, and he went into the Most Holy Place once for all time. So he set us free forever.
The blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a young cow sprinkled on people who were unclean, made their bodies clean.

So the blood of Christ will do so much more! Through the Spirit that lives forever, he offered himself to God as a perfect sacrifice. His blood will clean our consciences from actions that lead to death, so that we can serve the living God.

That is why Christ brings a new covenant between God and people. His death sets people free from the sins they did under the first covenant. So those whom God has called can receive what he promised: a gift that lasts forever.
When someone leaves a will, it must be proved that the person who made it has died.
A will only takes effect after a death. It never works while the person who made it is still alive.
That is why even the first covenant was not started without blood.
Moses told all the people every command in the law. Then he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, red wool and branches of hyssop, and sprinkled the book of the law and all the people.
He said, "This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded you to keep."
In the same way, he sprinkled blood on the tent of worship and on everything used in worship.
The law says that almost everything must be made clean with blood. And without blood being poured out, sins cannot be forgiven.
So the copies of the things in heaven had to be made clean by these sacrifices. But the things in heaven needed much better sacrifices.
Christ did not go into a holy place made by human hands, which was only a copy of the real one. He went into heaven itself, and now he stands before God for us.
He did not go in to offer himself again and again, like the high priest who goes into the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.
If that were so, Christ would have had to suffer many times since the world was made. But now, at the end of the ages, he has come once for all time to take away sin by sacrificing himself.
Everyone must die once, and after that comes judgment.
In the same way, Christ was offered once to take away the sins of many people. He will come a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.
